content: Active monitoring of adverse events associated with preventive chemotherapy (PC) for Taenia solium should be incorporated into randomized controlled trials, observational studies, and implementation or evaluation studies. The optimal observation period for accurately reporting adverse events following PC should be clearly defined. High-quality randomized controlled trials are needed to document the safety and drug interactions of simultaneous administration of niclosamide (NICL) or praziquantel (PZQ) for T. solium taeniasis with albendazole (ALB) or mebendazole for soil-transmitted helminths (STH). Mebendazole, administered as a single 500 mg dose, is also suitable for PC programs targeting STH control, and its interactions with NICL and PZQ warrant further investigation. Drug combinations, such as PZQ for T. solium taeniasis with ALB or mebendazole for STH, and NICL for taeniasis with ALB or mebendazole for STH, should be evaluated in other at-risk groups, including women of reproductive age. The value of PC for T. solium taeniasis to participants should be assessed, alongside economic evaluations (e.g., cost-utility, cost-effectiveness, or cost-benefit analyses) that consider the broader community impact. Additionally, the acceptability of PC for T. solium taeniasis among key stakeholders, including the affected communities, should be evaluated. The guideline for preventive chemotherapy for the control of T. solium taeniasis will be disseminated electronically in PDF format via the WHO and PAHO websites. The English version will be released first, followed by a Spanish translation, with French and Portuguese translations dependent on funding availability or limited to executive summaries. Dissemination will occur through a wide network of international partners, including WHO country and regional offices, ministries of health, collaborating centers, schools of public health and medicine, other United Nations agencies, and non-governmental organizations. Webinars and regional, subregional, and country meetings will also be utilized for dissemination. WHO will support Member States in developing and updating national strategies based on this guideline. Emphasis will be placed on engaging affected communities to inform implementation. The guideline is expected to remain valid until at least 2025 unless significant new evidence necessitates earlier revision.
